title: heal-attempt/1 (DEC-0191): one attempt of a product, dashboard or report to repair itself, and its outcome
description: What a product records each time it acts on a failing agent-health/1 check of its own: the episode, the attempt's number, the fix it called or why it called none, the outcome and the check's state after. Counts, kinds and codes only (DEC-0157): no account label, path, session id, host name or free text, so every object is closed. Semantic rule FAC-SEM-188. docs/specification/agent-health.md#self-healing-dec-0191.

product.description: The product, agent, dashboard or report that repaired itself, by its product id (DEC-0016).

check.description: The id of the agent-health/1 check the attempt acted on.

episode.description: The episode key <product>:<check id>@<YYYY-MM-DD> (HL-6, episodeKey), the UTC day of the reading that opened it; the product and check id are this record's (FAC-SEM-188).

attempt.description: The attempt's number within the episode: at most three automatic attempts (HEAL-2).

at.description: When the attempt ended, whole Unix seconds.

action.description: The fix the product called: an MCP tool of its own or a board capability of its owning project, or null when it called none (outcome skipped-human, skipped-gated or escalated without a call).

outcome.description: recovered: the check reads ok after the fix; not-recovered: the fix ran and the check is still bad; escalated: handed to the owning project or the person, once per episode (HEAL-4); skipped-human: the fix is a human step, never called for the person; skipped-gated: the fix would spend money, delete, publish or act on another product, so it was not called (HEAL-3).

after.description: The check's state read again after the attempt (agent-health/1 HL-2).

to.description: Where an escalated episode went: the owning project's board capability, or the operator channel. Present exactly when outcome is escalated (FAC-SEM-188).
